title: Tensor associativity for the integral reduction tower
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, S a scheme, and M,N objects of the derived category of internal integral modules [sk-def-pe-derived-completion, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. The canonical integral reduction tower of N followed by tensorLeft M is naturally isomorphic to the canonical integral reduction tower of M tensor N. This includes all transition morphisms, without completeness or dualizability hypotheses.

source.place: First paragraph: tensor commutes with reduction modulo powers of the uniformizer by associativity of the derived tensor product.

proof.text: Choose a native K-flat representative P of each derived object K. The localization lax tensorator is invertible with K-flat left argument. Combine its naturality with the single-complex tensor isomorphism to obtain K tensor B[0] naturally isomorphic to Q(P tensor B).

The strict scalar realization for P supplies the isomorphism Q(P tensor B_n) to integralLevel(K,n) and its consecutive transition equation. Naturality of the preceding comparison and this equation give a natural isomorphism from the coefficient tower followed by tensorLeft K to derivedTower K.

Apply the tower comparison to N and M tensor N. Whisker the inverse first comparison by tensorLeft M, then compose with the inverse associator M tensor (N tensor B[0]) ≅ (M tensor N) tensor B[0] and the second tower comparison. Naturality of the associator proves the required natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Associativity sentence of the first paragraph, with coherent finite-reduction realization.

lean.statement:
theorem tensorIntegralReductionTower
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (M N : DerivedCategory (Modules l E S)) :
    Nonempty (derivedTower l E S N ⋙ tensorLeft M ≅ derivedTower l E S (M ⊗ N))
